name: Paclitaxel + Cisplatin (or Carboplatin) + Bevacizumab for Recurrent/Metastatic Cervical Cancer (GOG-240)
histology: cervical squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, or adenosquamous carcinoma

biomarkers.note: The paclitaxel/platinum/bevacizumab regimen is not biomarker gated. PD-L1 (combined positive score) is tested to guide addition of pembrolizumab (a separate protocol). Bevacizumab is an anti-VEGF antibody, not biomarker selected.

lineOfTherapy: first-line systemic therapy for persistent, recurrent, or metastatic (FIGO stage IVB) cervical cancer

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: persistent, recurrent, or metastatic (stage IVB) cervical carcinoma
eligibilityCriteria.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
eligibilityCriteria.locator: lines 171368 to 171381 (GOG-240: paclitaxel-cisplatin or paclitaxel-topotecan, with or without bevacizumab, in primary stage IVB or recurrent/persistent disease)

drugs.name: PACLitaxel

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: lines 171368 to 171381 (GOG-240 paclitaxel-cisplatin plus bevacizumab); per-drug doses not printed in the cited source

drugs.notes: PACLitaxel is a component of the GOG-240 regimen (DeVita 12th ed. lines 171368 to 171381; regimen also cross-referenced at line 173802). The cited sources name the regimen but do NOT print the paclitaxel dose, schedule, basis, or unit; all are set to VERIFY pending a dosing source. Corticosteroid plus H1/H2 antihistamine premedication per labeling. Tall man per ISMP.

drugs.name: CISplatin

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: lines 171360 to 171381 (GOG-240: cisplatin doublet; cisplatin remains the key drug for platinum-naive patients); per-drug dose not printed

drugs.notes: CISplatin (carboplatin is an accepted substitute per NCCN CERV-F Carboplatin/Paclitaxel + Bevacizumab) is the platinum component of the GOG-240 doublet. The cited sources do NOT print the cisplatin dose/schedule; basis, dosePerUnit, unit, and days are VERIFY. Requires hydration and nephro/oto/neuro monitoring. Tall man per ISMP.

drugs.name: Bevacizumab

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: lines 171364 to 171381 (GOG-240: addition of bevacizumab significantly prolonged median OS 16.8 vs 13.3 months); per-drug dose not printed

drugs.notes: Bevacizumab is added to the doublet per GOG-240 (DeVita 12th ed. lines 171364 to 171381). The cited cervical sources do NOT print the bevacizumab dose/schedule; basis, dosePerUnit, unit, and days are VERIFY. No dose cap. Blood-pressure and proteinuria surveillance; GOG-240 reported higher grade 2+ hypertension, grade 3+ VTE, and grade 2+ fistula with bevacizumab (line 171377 to 171381).

premedications.name: PACLitaxel premedication
premedications.notes: corticosteroid plus H1 and H2 antihistamine premedication per paclitaxel labeling.

premedications.name: Cisplatin hydration
premedications.notes: IV hydration before and after cisplatin.

supportiveCare: bevacizumab: hypertension and proteinuria surveillance; bleeding, thromboembolism, and GI-perforation/fistula precautions.

monitoring: peripheral neuropathy assessment for PACLitaxel and cisplatin
bevacizumab: blood pressure and urine protein at each visit; monitor for fistula, VTE, and bleeding

doseModificationRules.condition: uncontrolled hypertension, grade 3+ proteinuria, fistula, GI perforation, or serious bleeding
doseModificationRules.text: Hold or permanently discontinue bevacizumab per anti-VEGF safety guidance; physician decides.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: lines 171364 to 171381 (GOG-240 phase III 2x2 factorial: paclitaxel-cisplatin or paclitaxel-topotecan +/- bevacizumab; bevacizumab prolonged OS); line 173802 (cisplatin/paclitaxel/bevacizumab per GOG-240)

guideline.locator: Systemic Therapy for Cervical Cancer, Recurrent or Metastatic, First-Line: Cisplatin/Paclitaxel + Bevacizumab (category 1) and Carboplatin/Paclitaxel + Bevacizumab (CERV-F 1 of 4); NCCN names the regimen but does not print per-drug doses

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for the GOG-240 paclitaxel + cisplatin (or carboplatin) + bevacizumab regimen for persistent, recurrent, or metastatic (stage IVB) cervical cancer (StewardMD reference disease cervical_cancer, subtype #42). DeVita 12th ed. lines 171364 to 171381 establish the GOG-240 phase III trial (paclitaxel-cisplatin or paclitaxel-topotecan, with or without bevacizumab; bevacizumab prolonged median OS from 13.3 to 16.8 months) and Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Cervical Cancer v2.2026 (CERV-F) lists Cisplatin/Paclitaxel + Bevacizumab (category 1) and Carboplatin/Paclitaxel + Bevacizumab as first-line recurrent/metastatic options. However, NEITHER cited source prints per-drug doses, schedules, or cycle length for this regimen; therefore every dose field (paclitaxel, cisplatin, bevacizumab basis/dosePerUnit/unit/days) plus cycleLengthDays and cycles are set to VERIFY and listed in verifyFields, pending a dosing source. No dose was invented or inferred. Bevacizumab has no dose cap and requires blood-pressure and proteinuria surveillance; cisplatin requires hydration and nephro/oto/neuro monitoring. ISMP tall man applied (CISplatin, PACLitaxel). This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
